content.text: patch (pætʃ ) Word forms: plural, 3rd person singular present tense patches , present participle patching , past tense, past participle patched 1. countable noun A patch on a surface is a part of it that is different in appearance from the area around it. ...the bald patch on the top of his head. There was a small patch of blue in the gray clouds. 2. countable noun A patch of land is a small area of land where a particular plant or crop grows. ...a patch of land covered in forest. ...the little vegetable patch in her backyard. 3. countable noun A patch is a piece of material that you use to cover a hole in something. ...jackets with patches on the elbows. 4. countable noun A patch is a small piece of material that you wear to cover an injured eye. She went to the hospital and found him lying down with a patch over his eye. 5. transitive verb If you patch something that has a hole in it, you repair it by fastening a patch over the hole. He and Walker patched the barn roof. One of the mechanics took off the damaged tire, and took it back to the station to be patched. 6. countable noun A patch is a piece of computer program code written as a temporary solution for dealing with a computer virus and distributed by the makers of the original program. [computing] Older machines will need a software patch to correct the date. Collins COBUILD Advanced Learner’s Dictionary. Copyright © HarperCollins Publishers American English pronunciation !
